threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You think the 106 bus runs on time because you saw one arrive at 10:03. Welcome to Stoke Newington. It’s a game of patience.
Caught a night bus from Croydon the other week. A couple of blokes were loudly debating if a kebab counts as breakfast. Only in South London!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a pigeon steal a bratwurst from a tourist's hand at Tempelhofer Feld. Classic Neukölln, where even the birds know how to hustle.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand that opens at 3 AM on weekends, serving late-night revelers their greasy fix with a side of Berliner charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their patience at Muni delays—everyone else freaks out when the bus is late, but we just know to grab a pupusa nearby.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy carrying a cat in a backpack on the 5-Fulton today, completely unfazed. Only in SF do we normalize that while dodging delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut in the late afternoon sun.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll catch them ordering a 'café con leche' at 5 PM like it's breakfast time, oblivious to the local rhythm.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'gentrification' is a bad word, not a badge of honor. The locals aren't quite as forgiving about that one.
Heard a guy on the 47 last night arguing with a pigeon over a chip. The bus stopped, and the pigeon just stared him down like it owned the place.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of toddlers arguing over a lost toy in the park, while their parents sipped coffee from the nearby kiosks. That's Neukölln life.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand open at 3 AM, serving up spicy sausages to midnight cyclists. Pure Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Real locals know to wear shoes that can handle a sudden BART shutdown—flip-flops don’t cut it when you’re forced to walk to 16th St.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus passengers with an accordion on Market St. Half the riders were tapping their feet, completely forgetting the delay.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the plazas, but the real heart beats in the back alleys where the local bars pour vermut like it's water.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them struggling with the metro map while eyeing the T10 card machine like it's a puzzle box. It's the classic lost-in-translation look.
